newsitem.title: BULGARIA: PRESS DIGEST - BULGARIAN BUSINESS WEEKLIES-JULY 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - BULGARIAN BUSINESS WEEKLIES-JULY 14.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Bulgarian business weeklies on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

-- The International Monetary Fund (IMF) board of directors will review Bulgaria's performance at its July 16 meeting and is expected to decide on the disbursement of a second $130-140 million tranche to Sofia under an IMF funding agreement sealed in mid-April.

-- Ahmed Dogan, the leader of Bulgaria's ethnic Turks Movement for Rights and Freedoms, said he was going to lobby in the parliament for the country's biggest private conglomerate Multigroup because he saw its operation, which sometimes attracts controvercial publicity, favourable for the country's economy.

-- Russia's Gazprom rejected a direct gas supply contract with the Bulgarian government, pledging to supply natural gas to Bulgaria only through its local joint-stock companies Topenergy and Overgas Inc, of which it holds 50 percent, said Gasprom supervisory board member Bogdan Budzuliak, who was in Sofia for talks with government officials,

-- The State Fund for Reconstruction and Development (SFRD) will allocate 260 billion levs for guarantees to Bulgarian commercial banks to cover credits extended to state-owned firms to buy out wheat from this year's crop.
So far the State Savings Bank, Bulbank, United Bulgarian Bank, Expressbank, Hebrosbank and Central Co-operative Bank have said they will fund the buying out of grain.

-- The first two weeks after the introduction of a currency board in Bulgaria on July 1 showed that people had confidence in the fixed exchange rate regime, deputy central bank governor Martin Zaimov said in an interview.
He said some 270 million German marks had been bought up by the central bank so far and that personal and company lev deposits in commercial banks have grown.
-- The Sofia City Court postponed for September 23 its ruling on an insolvency case filed by the central bank against the First Private Bank (FPB), which was put in receivership in May last year.

The central bank retracted the FPB banking licence two months ago citing the bank's failure to collect loans and repay debts of over 200 billion levs to its major creditors during the one-year period of receivership.

-- A Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) official said that the end of March 1988 would be the most likely deadline for the local commercial banks to meet BNB's minimum capital requirement of ten billion levs for full banking licence.
-- Bulgaria's tobacco production has fallen drasticaly to 40,000 tonnes in 1996 compared to 80,000 tonnes in 1990 and 160,000 tonnes in 1975.
-- France's biggest private bank Societe Generale opened its first branch in Sofia to service corporate clients operating in Bulgaria, general manager of the bank's Sofia branch Robert Frank said.
